witnesses.rationale: The exhaustive table always supplies a Word's exact declared arity (scripts/generate-semantics-table.mjs builds one operand per domain position), so no cell can ever be short an operand. Running ADD alone is the whole witness.

The exhaustive table only ever emits well-formed programs (one literal or Word name per domain position, then the Word); a program that fails to tokenize/parse at all is a different axis the table has no domain for. An unclosed vector literal is the simplest witness.

DEF's name-position domain representatives (textShort etc.) all happen to already be well-formed symbol lexemes, so the table never exercises a string that tokenizer::is_symbol_token_lexeme rejects. The empty string is not a name.
No domain representative names a live Core Word, so op_def_inner's Core-vocabulary refusal never fires in the table. Redefining ADD is the witness.
BIND's name-position domain representatives are never a live Core or User Word name, so the table never reaches check_bindable_name's refusal. 'ADD' is a Core Word.

Requires two statements sharing state (a live binding, then a DEF of the same name) — the exhaustive table only ever runs one Word against fresh domain literals, so no single cell can set up a binding for a second statement to conflict with.

Requires three statements: define A, define B referencing A, then try to redefine A while B still depends on it. Multi-statement dependency state is outside the one-Word-one-tuple table by construction (Phase 4 pitfall A’s own example).

The exact case Phase 4 pitfall A names: a DEF body that names the very word being defined. The table never writes a word body that references anything but core words and domain literals, so it cannot construct this on its own.

witnesses.source: [ 1 COLLECT [ 0 0 ] GET EXEC EXEC ] 1 COLLECT [ 0 0 ] GET EXEC EXEC
witnesses.rationale: Needs a block that builds a copy of itself and runs it, which takes several Words in sequence; the table runs one Word on one tuple of domain representatives and never writes such a program. The block runs once as written, then runs its copy, which is built from data, and that copy runs another — the second run built from data is the refusal.

MAP's element block runs with control arity of its own — the table's domain tuples only ever supply MAP's own two declared operands (a vector and a block), never a block whose *body* violates the ( x -- x ) contract MAP requires of it, since the block bodies the table writes are never anything but its own placeholder-free structure.

The table always runs under the native CLI's default step budget (12,180,000 — docs/dev/mcp-host-profiles.md), which no single-Word cell can plausibly exhaust. --step-limit is the one ceiling the CLI lets a caller shrink directly, so a 4-step program under a 1-step budget reaches it cheaply.

max_numeric_literal_digits (4,096, identical on every host profile per docs/dev/mcp-host-profiles.md) is a property of one literal's own text, which none of the table's domain representatives are long enough to cross — a 4,097-digit literal is the cheapest possible witness and needs no profile override.

The exhaustive table only ever runs a Word that exists, so no cell reaches a name that resolves to nothing. It used to reach this id indirectly: the higher-order Words took a String as their code operand, so a cell handing MAP the text domain looked up a Word named 'a' and answered unknownWord. That spelling is gone (LANG.SOURCE.CODE — code is a Vector, and a computed name defeated the acyclicity check LANG.DICTIONARY.ACYCLIC rests on), and those cells now answer notExecutable, which is what MAP's own contract declares. Writing an undefined name is the direct witness, and always was the honest one.

The exhaustive table's vector representatives are one element long, so they are trivially in order and BSEARCH's order check never fires there. An out-of-order three-element vector is the whole witness.
The exhaustive table reaches this through ABSENT's text representative too; this witness pins the reason a program states, with the text it states.
The one Word that raises this category, with the text a program would give.
No domain representative is a Vector with a repeated element, so the exhaustive table never hands RECORD two equal keys. A two-key Vector naming one key twice is the witness.

Stated explicitly beside its registry entry even though the exhaustive table also reaches it: no domain representative is a Record, so every Record Word cell the table runs answers nonRecord, and a reader of this file should not have to infer that.

The exhaustive table hands CONTRACT every domain representative, so the category is reached there too; stated beside its registry entry because a number is the operand that is neither a name nor a block. A String names a Word since 1.0.0-beta.2 and is no longer this error.

witnesses.source:
#:contract DOUBLE inputs=2 outputs=1
[ 2 MUL ] 'DOUBLE' DEF 5 DOUBLE
witnesses.rationale: The exhaustive table never writes a `#:contract` directive, and the category is raised by the pre-execution check rather than by any Word. A declaration whose `inputs` the body contradicts is the simplest witness: `compute` refuses to run it, as `check` refuses to pass it.
